_comment: signal_modulation/05_test_design (2026-09-09): TOY reservoir to PROVE the fading-memory mechanism inside a single FDTD run. The real device is blocked by two timescales 8 orders apart: optics ~ps vs. pump recharge tau(4F3/2)=230 us = 7e10 t.u., so in every prior design the pre-loaded inversion only ever DEPLETES and never recovers within the run (rate_32 defaulted to 0 = frozen upper level). Here we deliberately shorten the excited-state lifetime to ps scale (rate_32 finite) so the full charge -> deplete -> recharge cycle fits in the FDTD window. Then a symbols drive (piecewise-constant random amplitudes, one per symbol_length) exercises the reservoir: each strong symbol bleaches the gain, the recharge partially refills it before the next, and the output carries a NONLINEAR, FADING-MEMORY dependence on recent inputs. UNITS: a=1 um so 1 t.u. = 3.33 fs. TIMESCALES: gammaE 5.3e-4 = 159 GHz gain bandwidth => modulation no faster than ~6 ps (~1800 t.u.), so symbol_length=2000 t.u. (6.7 ps). rate_32=2e-4 => excited-state lifetime tau_32 = 1/rate_32 = 5000 t.u. = 16.7 ps ~ 2.5 symbols, giving fading memory over a few symbols (the knob we set: memory depth ~ tau_32/symbol_length). This is UNPHYSICAL for real Nd:YAG (tau is really 230 us) but that is the point: it validates the pipeline in pure MEEP; the real us device is the same physics with the recharge adiabatically eliminated (self-consistent stationary approach, characterization/i_sat_search.py). PILOT: this run needs the usual first-run calibration - watch pop_monitor for the pumped steady inversion and its recharge time, and snap_point for the output responding to the symbol sequence; amp_range and pump amplitude will likely need one tuning pass to sit in the saturating regime. Backend MUST be meep (symbols = mp.CustomSource, no gpumeep equivalent). Based on design01 geometry (small crystal 20 um, single Ey signal guide, 808 nm pump from above).

crystal._comment: Nd:YAG gain, same 4-level SGMA coupling as design01 (SGMA 1.86e-5, N3_0 30 pre-inverted, gL ~ O(1) over 20 um). THE ONE CHANGE vs design01: rate_32=2e-4 gives the upper level a FINITE ps lifetime (16.7 t.u.*300... = 16.7 ps) instead of the frozen 230-us default, so the pump can actually recharge burned inversion within the run. rate_43/rate_21 stay the fast feeder/drain.

source_1._comment: reservoir input drive: piecewise-constant random amplitudes u(n) ~ U(amp_range), one per symbol_length, on the 1.064 um carrier. seed 0 => analysis regenerates the exact sequence (symbols_source.symbol_sequence) to build regression targets. amp_range spans ~linear to ~saturating around design01's amp 1.0 - tune after the pilot.

source_pump._comment: 808 nm CW pump from above (y-normal sheet on the crystal top edge), Ez orthogonal to the Ey signal. With rate_32 finite the pump now sets a STEADY inversion (pump-in vs rate_32-out balance) instead of just pre-loading it; amp 50 from design01, tune if the steady N3 sits too low/high.

snap_point._comment: exit output time trace - the reservoir readout. dt 2.0 resolves the symbol steps (symbol_length 2000) while keeping the trace light; envelope offline. This vs the input sequence is the fading-memory / nonlinearity proof.

pop_monitor._comment: inversion vs time - THE key plot for this toy: N3 should be seen bleaching on each strong symbol and RECHARGING between them (tau_32 = 5000 t.u.), i.e. actually recovering within the run, which no prior design could show.
